tasks.rationale: Translate general disjointness into containment or a probability bound, then distinguish a non-strict universal inequality from its reverse and strict alternatives, including the equality case. This is abstract transfer rather than direct substitution into a taught numerical example.
tasks.derivation: Disjointness gives A subset of complement B, so P(A) ≤ P(complement B): A holds for every case. Taking P(A)=0.2 and P(B)=0.3 makes P(A)=0.2 < 0.7=P(complement B), disproving B and D as universal statements. Taking complementary disjoint events with probabilities 0.4 and 0.6 gives equality, disproving C. D is in fact impossible for disjoint events; B holds only in the equality case. Native solution derives A from additivity and the upper bound 1.
